title: English Grammar Error Spotting - Articles & Prepositions
subject: English

questions.text: The loss of jobs is regarded by some as an necessary evil in the fight against inflation.
options: (b) is regarded by some as an necessary evil
questions.explanation: Use 'a' instead of 'an' before 'necessary evil'. 'necessary' does not start with a vowel sound, it starts with a consonant sound.

questions.text: It is a quarter to ten by my watch.
questions.explanation: Remove 'a' before 'quarter to ten'. We don't use an article before time expressions like 'quarter to ten'.

questions.text: Gita doesn't usually wear jewellery but yesterday she wore ring.
questions.explanation: 'ring' is a singular countable noun being mentioned for the first time. Hence, use 'a ring'.

questions.text: The police asked us about our movements on a night of crime.
questions.explanation: 'night of crime' refers to the specific night when the crime happened. Hence, use the definite article 'the night of crime'.

questions.text: In science the credit goes to a man who convinces the world, not to the man to whom the idea first occurs.
options: (a) In science the credit goes to a man
(c) not to the man to whom the idea first occurs
questions.explanation: The man who convinced the world is a specific person. Hence, use the definite article 'the man'.

questions.text: It is only after the match is over that people realize how exciting it is.
options: (c) that people realize how exciting it is
questions.explanation: We are not talking about a specific match. The meaning is that when any match is over, people realize how exciting it was. Hence, use 'a match'.

questions.text: Of the two sisters, she is better.
questions.explanation: When choosing one of two, we use comparative degree with 'the'. Hence, use 'the better'.

questions.text: It is unfortunate enough to lose few friends we make during our school days.
options: (b) to lose few friends we make
questions.explanation: We are talking about specific friends (the ones we make during school days). Hence, use 'the few friends'.

questions.text: There were a number of intelligent gentlemen at the party but it was Mr. Subramaniam, an eminent scientist, who remained centre of attraction.
options: (a) There were a number of intelligent gentlemen at the party
(b) but it was Mr. Subramaniam, an eminent scientist,
questions.explanation: 'centre of attraction' refers to a specific position. Hence, use 'the centre of attraction'.

questions.text: I have been informed that Mr. Sharma, the director and the chairman will visit Patna the following month.
options: (b) Mr. Sharma, the director and the chairman
(c) will visit Patna the following month
questions.explanation: Mr. Sharma is one person holding two positions. Hence, use only one 'the': 'the director and chairman'.

questions.text: He is the best worker of the factory but unfortunately least paid.
options: (b) the best worker of the factory
questions.explanation: 'least' is the superlative degree. Hence, use 'the least paid'.

questions.text: He has come out with an unique proposal for his friends.
questions.explanation: 'unique' starts with a consonant sound ('y' sound), so use 'a' instead of 'an'.

questions.text: When the house was set on the fire, all the people started shouting at the top of their voices.
options: (c) all the people started shouting at the top of their voices
questions.explanation: The correct phrase is 'set on fire', not 'set on the fire'.

questions.text: Little knowledge of medicine that he possessed proved to be a blessing for him when he was in great pain.
options: (c) proved to be a blessing for him when he was in great pain
questions.explanation: Here 'little' means 'some small amount' (not 'none'). Hence, use 'a little knowledge' or 'the little knowledge'.

questions.text: It was by a mistake that he injured her hand.
questions.explanation: The correct phrase is 'by mistake', not 'by a mistake'.

questions.text: These orders of the Manager may put the lives of two thousand workers in a danger.
options: (c) may put the lives of two thousand workers in a danger
questions.explanation: The correct phrase is 'in danger', not 'in a danger'.

questions.text: I inspired him to take the heart in all adverse situations and deserve to be called a real hero.
options: (c) in all adverse situations and deserve to be called a real hero
questions.explanation: The correct phrase is 'to take heart' (meaning 'to be encouraged'), not 'to take the heart'.

questions.text: The most happy marriage would be a union of a deaf man and a blind woman.
options: (c) a union of a deaf man and a blind woman
questions.explanation: We are talking about marriage in general, not a specific union. Hence, use 'union' without 'a' or use 'the union' if referring to a specific concept.

questions.text: John suggested to the children of his village that they should go to the school regularly and do their homework sincerely.
options: (b) the children of his village that they should
(c) go to the school regularly and do their homework sincerely
questions.explanation: When 'school' refers to the activity of studying, we don't use 'the'. Hence, 'go to school' is correct.

questions.text: Some people say that her husband is in the jail and so she lives alone.
options: (b) her husband is in the jail
questions.explanation: When 'jail' refers to the institution/punishment, we don't use 'the'. Hence, 'in jail' is correct.

questions.text: The Greek peoples are considered very brave.
questions.explanation: 'Peoples' means different ethnic groups. For the Greek nation, use 'the Greek people' or 'the Greeks'.

questions.text: His father asked him to go to the temple every morning.
questions.explanation: When 'temple' refers to worship/religious activity, we don't use 'the'. Hence, 'go to temple' is correct.

questions.text: There was little milk in the refrigerator and she gave it to her crying son.
options: (b) milk in the refrigerator and she gave it
questions.explanation: Here we mean 'some milk' (not 'no milk'). Hence, use 'a little milk'.

questions.text: He leads a very luxurious life so he goes to every part of India by a car.
options: (c) so he goes to every part of India by a car
questions.explanation: The correct phrase is 'by car', not 'by a car'.

questions.text: Thanks to an effort and persistence of the doctors, the victims of the blast have been able to start a normal life again.
options: (b) and persistence of the doctors, the victims of the blast
(c) have been able to start a normal life again
questions.explanation: 'Effort' is specific here (the doctors' effort). Hence, use 'the effort'.

questions.text: In a hour's time I will be back but now I have to go.
options: (c) but now I have to go
questions.explanation: 'hour' starts with a vowel sound, so use 'an hour' instead of 'a hour'.

questions.text: Terrorist organizations kill innocent people to spread a violence.
questions.explanation: 'violence' is an uncountable noun. We don't use 'a' with uncountable nouns. Hence, 'spread violence' is correct.

questions.text: Whole world is today facing the threat of extinction due to the inventions of Science.
options: (b) today facing the threat of extinction
(c) due to the inventions of Science
questions.explanation: Use 'the' before 'whole world': 'The whole world'.

questions.text: The answer to all the sufferings of human beings lies in the Science.
options: (c) human beings lies in the Science
questions.explanation: We don't use 'the' before names of subjects. Hence, 'in Science' is correct.

questions.text: The police should exercise their authority with little bit of sensitivity and humanity.
questions.explanation: Here we mean 'some small amount'. Hence, use 'a little bit' instead of 'little bit'.

questions.text: This is most important lesson which we will have to study very carefully.
options: (c) lesson which we will have to study very carefully
questions.explanation: 'most' is superlative degree. Hence, use 'the most important'.

questions.text: The Ganges is for North India what Krishna is for South India.
options: (c) what Krishna is for South India
questions.explanation: We use 'the' before names of rivers. Hence, 'the Krishna' is correct.

questions.text: I like to travel by the air as I am a very busy person.
options: (c) I am a very busy person
questions.explanation: The correct phrase is 'by air', not 'by the air'.

questions.text: The Chairman and the Trustee was removed from his post because he had misappropriated the fund.
options: (c) post because he had misappropriated the fund
questions.explanation: One person holds both positions. Hence, use only one 'the': 'The Chairman and Trustee'.

questions.text: She found herself in a trouble when she saw the stalker following her persistently.
options: (c) when she saw the stalker following her persistently
questions.explanation: 'trouble' is uncountable. We don't use 'a' with uncountable nouns. Hence, 'in trouble' is correct.

questions.text: All the people of India know that Gandhi ji was a very wise and a noble soul.
options: (c) Gandhi ji was a very wise and a noble soul
questions.explanation: When two adjectives describe the same person, use 'a' only before the first adjective. Hence, 'a very wise and noble soul'.

questions.text: The man is the only creature that is endowed with the art of humour.
options: (c) that is endowed with the art of humour
questions.explanation: When 'man' means mankind/human race, we don't use 'the'. Hence, 'Man is the only creature...'

questions.text: It is very difficult to find out the number of the creatures living on the earth.
options: (b) to find out the number of
(c) the creatures living on the earth
questions.explanation: We are not talking about specific creatures. Hence, remove 'the' before 'creatures'.

questions.text: While climbing the hill, to his amazement, the poor man found the box of pearls.
options: (c) poor man found the box of pearls
questions.explanation: The box of pearls was not known to the man. Hence, use 'a box of pearls' instead of 'the box of pearls'.

questions.text: The blast derailed the lives of many people but in an year time leaving apart the victims, no one remembered anything.
options: (a) The blast derailed the lives of many people but
(b) in an year time leaving apart the victims,
questions.explanation: 'year' starts with a consonant sound ('y' sound). Hence, use 'a year' instead of 'an year'.

questions.text: Cowards die several times, the braves die but once.
questions.explanation: 'brave' is an adjective. To refer to brave people, we say 'the brave', not 'braves'. 'Braves' is incorrect.

questions.text: Akbar became a heir to the throne at a young age of thirteen.
questions.explanation: 'heir' starts with a vowel sound (silent 'h'), so use 'an heir' instead of 'a heir'.

questions.text: The both brothers are safe now and are recuperating.
questions.explanation: The correct structure is 'Both the brothers' or 'Both brothers', not 'The both brothers'.

questions.text: When the principal entered the classroom all boys shook in their shoes.
options: (a) When the principal entered the classroom
questions.explanation: We are talking about specific boys (in that classroom). Hence, use 'all the boys'.

questions.text: Father in him could not bear the condition of his ailing daughter.
options: (b) could not bear the condition of
questions.explanation: When referring to a quality within a person, use 'the'. Hence, 'The father in him'.

questions.text: Let judge in you decide what punishment should be given to him.
options: (c) punishment should be given to him
questions.explanation: When referring to a quality within a person, use 'the'. Hence, 'Let the judge in you'.

questions.text: My teacher said that Sun is a star.
questions.explanation: We use 'the' before names of heavenly bodies. Hence, 'the Sun'.

questions.text: Due to its beauty Kashmir is known as Switzerland of India.
questions.explanation: When comparing to a country name in such expressions, we use 'the'. Hence, 'the Switzerland of India'.

questions.text: Most of the people of Southern India do not know the Hindi.
options: (a) Most of the people of Southern India
questions.explanation: We don't use 'the' before names of languages. Hence, 'Hindi' (without 'the').

questions.text: He went for the lunch at 1 p.m. and then returned.
questions.explanation: We don't use 'the' before meals (lunch, dinner, breakfast) in general. Hence, 'went for lunch'.

questions.text: The honesty is a virtue.
questions.explanation: We don't use articles before abstract nouns in general statements. Hence, 'Honesty is a virtue'.

questions.text: Every morning the Sun rises in east.
questions.explanation: We use 'the' before directions. Hence, 'in the east'.

questions.text: He is best player in India.
questions.explanation: 'best' is superlative degree. Hence, use 'the best player'.

questions.text: When I met him the couple of days back he was writing a new book.
options: (c) he was writing a new book
questions.explanation: We are not talking about a specific couple of days. Hence, use 'a couple of days'.
